question: Many people say technology has changed the way we enjoy music. What are some of the positive and negative effects of this change? Give your opinion with examples.
answer: I'd argue that technology has been a double-edged sword for music lovers. On the bright side, streaming platforms have made music incredibly accessible; for a small monthly fee, I can explore genres from all over the world that I never would have stumbled upon twenty years ago. Algorithms also give independent artists a fighting chance to reach listeners without a big label behind them. On the flip side, I think this convenience has made us more passive. Many people, myself included, tend to treat songs as background noise rather than sitting down and listening to an album from start to finish. There's also the issue of fair pay, since artists earn only a fraction of a cent per stream. So overall, I believe the benefits outweigh the drawbacks, but we should be more intentional about how we listen and support the musicians we love.

question: Tell me about a time when you cooked something that didn't turn out the way you expected. What went wrong, and what did you learn?
answer: Oh, I have a pretty embarrassing one. Last winter, I decided to host a small dinner party and, being a bit overconfident, I chose to make beef bourguignon for the first time, a French stew I'd only ever seen in videos. Everything seemed fine until I realized, about an hour before my guests arrived, that I'd misread the recipe and added a tablespoon of salt instead of a teaspoon. The stew was practically inedible. I panicked at first, but then I diluted it with extra broth, threw in some potatoes to soak up the salt, and served it with plenty of bread. Surprisingly, my friends said it was delicious, though I suspect they were just being kind. The biggest lesson I took away was to do a trial run before cooking something ambitious for other people, and to double-check measurements, no matter how confident I feel.

answer: Personally, I lean toward city life, at least for this stage of my life. question: Talk about how your neighborhood has changed over the past few years. What do you think about these changes, and why?
answer: Over the last five years, my neighborhood has gone through a pretty dramatic transformation. What used to be a row of old, family-run shops has largely been replaced by trendy cafes, co-working spaces, and a massive new apartment complex. On one hand, I appreciate the convenience; there's a gym and a supermarket just a few minutes' walk away, and the streets feel safer at night thanks to better lighting. On the other hand, the gentrification has pushed out many long-time residents and small business owners who simply couldn't keep up with the rising rent. The bakery I used to visit as a kid closed down last year, which honestly broke my heart. I think development is inevitable, but local governments should do more to protect the character of a community and the people who built it.

question: These days, many people travel abroad instead of traveling in Korea. Why do you think this is happening, and what is your opinion about it?
answer: I think there are several reasons behind this trend. First, budget airlines have made international flights surprisingly affordable, so a weekend in Osaka can sometimes cost less than a trip to Jeju. Second, social media plays a huge role, since people want to share unique experiences abroad. Third, domestic travel spots are often criticized for overpriced food and accommodation, which Koreans call 바가지. Personally, I enjoy both, but I think local tourism needs to become more competitive by improving service and keeping prices reasonable. Otherwise, the gap will only keep growing.
